title: Will the House vote on impeaching Pete Hegseth? Before Nov 14, 2026
rules: If the House has conducted any recorded vote on any resolution impeaching Pete Hegseth, any motion to table, refer, or postpone such a resolution, or any special rule that specifically refers to such a resolution after Issuance and before Nov 14, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
This includes:
Roll call votes
Recorded votes
Yea-and-nay votes
Electronic votes (in the House)
Division/standing votes

The following do NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion:
Voice votes where individual member positions are not recorded, including a motion to table, refer, or postpone that is agreed to by voice vote
Unanimous consent agreements without a recorded vote
Votes in committee, including any vote of the House Judiciary Committee
Procedural determinations by the presiding officer, including a ruling on whether a resolution is privileged, and any vote on an appeal of such a ruling
Deemed passage without an actual vote
A Member giving notice of intent to offer, reading, or introducing a resolution impeaching Pete Hegseth
A vote on adjourning or recessing, or on any special rule or other measure that does not specifically refer to a resolution impeaching Pete Hegseth
A vote on an amendment to a resolution impeaching Pete Hegseth
A vote on a resolution that only authorizes or directs an impeachment inquiry or investigation of Pete Hegseth

For clarity, each of the following DOES satisfy the Payout Criterion, whatever the outcome of the vote:
A vote on adopting a resolution impeaching Pete Hegseth, or on any article of it
A vote on a motion to table, refer, or postpone a resolution impeaching Pete Hegseth
A vote on whether the House will consider a resolution impeaching Pete Hegseth, or on ordering the previous question on it
A vote on a special rule that specifically refers to a resolution impeaching Pete Hegseth, including ordering the previous question on that rule, whether the rule provides for the resolution's consideration, lays it on the table, refers it, or delays or waives the time for its consideration

blind.reasoning: Rep. Massie has promised to force a privileged vote on impeaching Hegseth in the first week of the lame-duck session, which begins Nov 9. Once he gives notice, the Speaker must schedule a vote within two legislative days, and a recorded motion to table would count. The window before the Nov 13 deadline is only about four days, and Veterans Day falls in it, so any delay in Massie's notice, a light House schedule, leadership stalling, or Hegseth leaving office first could push the vote past the deadline.
blind.falsifier: Massie gives notice later than Tuesday Nov 10, the House leaves before the two-legislative-day window closes, or Trump fires Hegseth or he resigns before a vote, so no recorded vote happens by Nov 13.

final.reasoning: The market's 0.415 suggests more timing risk than I assumed, so I lowered my estimate to 0.48. That still sits above the 0.42 ask, given Massie's stated 'week one' plan and the two-legislative-day rule forcing a vote soon after his notice.
